items.question: Monthly pay: basic ₹30,000, DA ₹10,000, HRA ₹12,000. EPF is 12% of basic plus DA for both employee and employer. Professional tax ₹200 and TDS ₹1,500 are deducted. Net pay to the employee is:
items.explanation: Gross ₹52,000. Only the employee's EPF of 12% on basic plus DA (₹4,800) is deducted, with PT and TDS. The employer's share is the employer's own expense, not a deduction.

why_not.C: Also deducts the employer's EPF share, which the employer bears itself.
why_not.B: Charges EPF on gross pay including HRA instead of basic plus DA.
why_not.D: Forgets the EPF deduction and deducts only PT and TDS.

items.exam_tip: Employer's PF contribution is a cost to the employer; only the employee's share comes out of pay.
items.reviewer_note: Rates are stated in the question, so no outside rate is assumed.
check_notes: Writer: Rates are stated in the question, so no outside rate is assumed.

items.question: A company has ₹10 lakh in a revaluation reserve, ₹6 lakh in securities premium and ₹4 lakh in free general reserve. It wants to issue fully paid bonus shares without receiving cash. Which reserve can NOT be used?
items.explanation: Bonus shares may be paid from free reserves, securities premium or capital redemption reserve. A revaluation reserve is an unrealised gain, so it cannot be capitalised for bonus shares.

why_not.C: Thinks premium is restricted; it can fund fully paid bonus shares.
why_not.D: Free reserves are the main source of bonus shares.
why_not.A: Capital redemption reserve can be used for fully paid bonus shares.

items.exam_tip: Bonus needs realised sources only. Revaluation reserve is unrealised, so it is never capitalised.
items.reviewer_note: Option D: CRR use for fully paid bonus is permitted under Companies Act s.69 and s.63; verify wording.
check_notes: Writer: Option D: CRR use for fully paid bonus is permitted under Companies Act s.69 and s.63; verify wording.
Checker: Option A (capital redemption reserve) is not among the company's stated balances, though the law permits it. Some students may be confused, but it is still a valid distractor.
Checker: The question does not say that the Companies Act 2013 applies. This is a wording polish only.
Checker: 'Free general reserve' is a slightly odd term. 'Free reserves' would be more standard.

items.question: Under Ind AS 36, a machine has a carrying amount of ₹60,00,000. Its fair value is ₹55,00,000, costs of disposal are ₹3,00,000 and its value in use is ₹54,00,000. What impairment loss is recognised?
items.explanation: Recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs of disposal (₹52,00,000) and value in use (₹54,00,000), so ₹54,00,000. Loss = ₹60,00,000 - ₹54,00,000 = ₹6,00,000.

working.label: Fair value less costs of disposal

why_not.D: Used fair value of ₹55,00,000 and ignored the costs of disposal.
why_not.A: Used fair value less costs of disposal, the lower figure, instead of the higher recoverable amount.
why_not.B: Added disposal costs to value in use, giving ₹57,00,000 as recoverable amount.

items.exam_tip: Recoverable amount = HIGHER of FVLCD and value in use. Loss = carrying amount minus recoverable amount.
items.calculation:
fvlcd = 5500000 - 300000
viu = 5400000
recoverable = max(fvlcd, viu)
answer = 6000000 - recoverable
